question_text: Select the group in which all organisms have the same mode of nutrition.
options: Cuscuta, yeast, legumes, leeches and tapeworm
Cactus, ticks, lice, leeches and cow
Cuscuta, ticks, lice, leeches and tapeworm
Cactus, grass, lice, lion and tapeworm
answer_text: Cuscuta, ticks, lice, leeches and tapeworm
answer_explanation: All listed organisms are parasites and obtain nutrition from a living host.

question_text: Which of the following options indicates the products formed after breakdown of the glucose in our muscle cells when there is lack of oxygen?
options: Ethanol + carbon dioxide + Energy
Lactic acid + Energy
Lactic acid + carbon monoxide + Energy
Carbon dioxide + Water + Energy
answer_text: Lactic acid + Energy
answer_explanation: In oxygen-deficient muscle cells, glucose undergoes anaerobic respiration to form lactic acid with release of a small amount of energy.

question_text: Which of the following is a correct combination of function and part of the brain?
options: Posture and balance: Cerebrum
Salivation: Medulla in midbrain
Hunger: Pons in hindbrain
Blood pressure: Medulla in hindbrain
answer_text: Blood pressure: Medulla in hindbrain
answer_explanation: The medulla oblongata, a part of the hindbrain, controls involuntary activities including blood pressure.

question_text: The blood glucose level in a patient was very high. It may be due to inadequate secretion of:
options: growth hormone from pituitary gland
oestrogen from ovary
insulin from pituitary gland
insulin from pancreas
answer_text: insulin from pancreas
answer_explanation: Insulin secreted by pancreatic beta cells lowers blood glucose; inadequate insulin causes abnormally high blood sugar.

question_text: In a cross between black furred rabbit (B) and white furred rabbit (b), all offspring were found to have black fur. What can be inferred about the genetic makeup of the parent rabbits?
options: BB X bb
Bb X Bb
Bb X bb
bb X bb
answer_text: BB X bb
answer_explanation: A homozygous dominant black rabbit crossed with a homozygous recessive white rabbit produces only Bb black offspring.

question_text: Which are the correct statements related to ozone? (i) Ozone layer helps in increasing the UV radiations reaching earth. (ii) Ozone is a deadly poison. (iii) Ozone layer shields the earth from UV radiations. (iv) Ozone layer prevents UV rays which cause skin cancer. (v) Ozone is formed with the help of Chloroflurocarbons.
options: (i), (ii), (iii)
(ii), (iii), (iv)
(iii), (iv), (v)
answer_text: (ii), (iii), (iv)
answer_explanation: Ozone is toxic near the ground but the stratospheric ozone layer absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation, reducing risks such as skin cancer.

question_text: Which of the following human activities has resulted in an increase of non - biodegradable substances?
options: Organic farming
Increase in tree plantation
Use of plastic as packaging material
Composting of kitchen waste
answer_text: Use of plastic as packaging material
answer_explanation: Most plastics are non-biodegradable and accumulate in the environment.

question_text: Assertion (A): Tallness of a pea plant is controlled by an enzyme. Reason (R): The gene for that enzyme makes proteins which help the plant to be tall.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, and R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
answer_text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
answer_explanation: Genes express themselves through proteins or enzymes. The relevant enzyme promotes growth processes that produce tallness.

question_text: Assertion (A): Vulture will always have the least amount of pesticides in a food chain. Reason (R): Vulture occupies the last trophic level and it gets only 10% of energy of the previous trophic level.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, and R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
answer_text: A is false but R is true.
answer_explanation: Persistent pesticides biomagnify, so a vulture at the last trophic level has the highest, not the least, pesticide concentration. The 10% law about energy transfer is true.

question_text: Unlike animals, plants do not have any excretory products as they do not eat food. Comment upon the statement with justification.
answer_text: The statement is incorrect. Plants also produce excretory products during metabolism. Oxygen from photosynthesis, carbon dioxide from respiration and excess water are removed through stomata/lenticels; other wastes are stored in vacuoles, leaves, bark or as gums and resins and are removed when these parts are shed.
answer_explanation: Plants make their own food, but cellular reactions still generate wastes. They eliminate or store these substances by diffusion, transpiration and sequestration in tissues.

question_text: Students to attempt either option A or B. A. How many chambers are there in the heart of the following organisms? How is mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood prevented in their body? (i) Fishes (ii) Humans OR B. Explain the mechanism by which the water is transported in plants?
answer_text:
Option A:
(i) Fish: two-chambered heart—one atrium and one ventricle. Only deoxygenated blood passes through the heart; oxygenated blood from gills goes directly to the body, so mixing does not occur in the heart.
(ii) Humans: four-chambered heart—two atria and two ventricles. A complete septum separates the right and left sides and prevents mixing.

OR

Option B:
Water and minerals enter root hairs by osmosis and active absorption, move into the xylem and rise through xylem vessels. Root pressure assists, but the main force is transpiration pull created by evaporation from leaves, aided by cohesion and adhesion of water molecules.
answer_explanation: Different circulatory designs prevent mixing according to the organism's needs. In plants, xylem provides a continuous pathway and transpiration creates the upward pull.

question_text: About 100 acres of forest land was declared as Natural reserve park. The following organisms were predominant in the Natural reserve park: . rabbit, frog, grass, fish, fox, water insects, zebra, peacock, snake, trees, bird, owl, insects, tiger, vulture, duck. Create a food web comprising two separate food chains with different producers by using the above data.
answer_text:
One valid food web is:
Grass → rabbit → fox → tiger
Grass → insects → frog → snake → owl
Trees → insects → bird → owl
Trees → zebra → tiger
The two chains begin with different producers, for example: Grass → rabbit → fox and Trees → insects → bird → owl.
answer_explanation: Arrows show transfer of food and energy from producer to consumer. Interlinked chains form a food web and may share predators.

question_text: Draw and explain how the nerve cells help in transmission of impulses? 3
answer_text:
A labelled neuron should show dendrites, cell body with nucleus, axon and axon terminals/synapse.
1. Dendrites receive a stimulus and generate an electrical impulse.
2. The impulse travels through the cell body and along the axon.
3. At the axon terminal, neurotransmitters cross the synapse and initiate an impulse in the next neuron or an effector.
answer_explanation: A neuron transmits information electrically along its membrane and chemically across a synapse, ensuring one-way communication between cells.

question_text: In a genetic experiment, plants with pure round green seeds (RRyy) were crossed with plants with wrinkled yellow seeds (rrYY). (i) Show the gametes formed when F1 was self-pollinated. (ii) A total of 144 seeds were produced which developed into saplings. Show the ratio in which these traits are independently inherited in these144 sapling.
answer_text:
P: RRyy × rrYY
Gametes: Ry and rY
F₁: all RrYy (round yellow).
On self-pollination: RrYy × RrYy. Each F₂ plant forms four gametes: RY, Ry, rY and ry.
The F₂ phenotypic ratio is 9 round yellow : 3 round green : 3 wrinkled yellow : 1 wrinkled green.
Out of 144 saplings:
Round yellow = 9/16 × 144 = 81
Round green = 3/16 × 144 = 27
Wrinkled yellow = 3/16 × 144 = 27
Wrinkled green = 1/16 × 144 = 9.
answer_explanation: The two gene pairs assort independently during gamete formation, producing the standard dihybrid 9:3:3:1 phenotypic ratio.

question_text: Neha consumed boiled sweet potatoes and boiled eggs for breakfast. Help her to understand some steps in the process of digestion of the food taken by her by answering the questions given below. Attempt either subpart A or B. A. Which of these food items is rich in proteins? In which part of the alimentary canal is the digestion of this component initia ted? Name the enzymes, conditions required and the glands associated with the digestion here. OR B. Which of these food items contains fats? How is it digested? C. Which of these food items is rich in starch? How is its digestion initiated? D. The figure given below represents parts of the human alimentary canal. Which of these parts will have the maximum amount of digested food as soon as the process of digestion is completed? . For visually impaired students D. How will the digested food be taken up by the alimentary canal?
answer_text:
A. Boiled egg is rich in protein. Protein digestion begins in the stomach. Gastric glands secrete hydrochloric acid, pepsin and mucus; HCl provides an acidic medium and activates pepsin, which digests proteins into smaller peptides.

OR

B. Egg contains fat. In the small intestine, bile from the liver emulsifies fat and provides an alkaline medium; lipase, mainly from the pancreas, breaks fats into fatty acids and glycerol.

C. Sweet potato is rich in starch. Digestion begins in the mouth where salivary amylase acts on starch in a nearly neutral medium and converts it into sugars.

D. The small intestine has the maximum amount of digested food after digestion is completed. The digested nutrients are absorbed through villi into blood capillaries; fatty acids and glycerol enter lacteals.
answer_explanation: Different food components require specific enzymes and conditions. Digestion is completed and most absorption occurs in the small intestine because of its enzymes and large villus-lined surface.

question_text: Attempt either option A or B. A. Puneet wanted to grow banana plants. (i) Based on your knowledge on plant reproduction should he opt for seeds or any alternate method of reproduction. Justify your answer. (ii) Offsprings of a banana plant usually show very little variation. What causes variation and are variations good or bad? Justify. OR B. Annie was conducting research on the number of fruits produced by watermelon under different conditions. She grew 25 watermelon plants each in both glass house A and B. She introduced pollinators in glass house A only. (i) What difference will she observe in the number of fruits produced in the two glass houses? Explain with reason. (ii) List 3 changes that will occur in a flower once it gets fertilized. Section – B
answer_text:
Option A:
(i) Puneet should use vegetative propagation, such as suckers or tissue culture, rather than seeds. Cultivated bananas are commonly seedless; vegetative propagation is rapid and produces plants retaining desirable parental characters.
(ii) Very little variation occurs because asexual reproduction involves one parent and no fusion of gametes. Variations arise mainly from DNA-copying errors/mutations and, in sexual reproduction, recombination. Variations may be advantageous, neutral or harmful; useful variations help survival under changing conditions and form the basis of evolution.

OR

Option B:
(i) Glass house A will produce more fruits because introduced pollinators transfer pollen to stigmas and increase pollination and fertilisation. Glass house B will produce fewer or no fruits depending on natural/self-pollination.
(ii) After fertilisation: the zygote develops into an embryo; ovules become seeds; the ovary enlarges into a fruit and its wall forms the pericarp. Petals, sepals, stamens, style and stigma usually wither and fall.
answer_explanation: Vegetative propagation produces genetically similar clones, whereas sexual reproduction and mutations generate variation. Fruit formation in flowering plants depends on successful pollination followed by fertilisation.

question_text: Which of the following equations represent redox reactions and what are the values for ‘p’ and ‘q’ in these equations? Equation 1: Fe2O3(s) + 2Al(s) Al2O3 (s) + p Fe(l) + heat Equation 2: 2C4H10(g) + 13O2(g) → 8CO2(g)+ q H2O(g)
options: Only equation 1 is a redox reaction, p =1 and q=3
Both equations 1 and 2 are redox reactions, p= 2 and q=4
Only equation 2 is a redox reaction, p= 2 and q= 10
Both equations 1 and 2 are redox reactions, p= 2 and q=10
answer_text: Both equations 1 and 2 are redox reactions, p= 2 and q=10
answer_explanation: Balancing gives Fe₂O₃ + 2Al → Al₂O₃ + 2Fe and 2C₄H₁₀ + 13O₂ → 8CO₂ + 10H₂O. Oxidation and reduction occur simultaneously in both.

question_text: Four statements about the reactions of oxides with dilute hydrochloric acid and aqueous sodium hydroxide are listed. I. Aluminium oxide reacts with both dilute hydrochloric acid and aqueous sodium hydroxide. II. Calcium oxide reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid and aqueous sodi um hydroxide. III. Zinc oxide reacts with both dilute hydrochloric acid and aqueous sodium hydroxide. IV. Sulphur dioxide does not react with either dilute hydrochloric acid or aqueous sodium hydroxide. Which statements are correct?
options: I and II
I and III
II and IV
III and IV
answer_text: I and III
answer_explanation: Aluminium oxide and zinc oxide are amphoteric and react with both acids and bases. Calcium oxide is basic, while sulphur dioxide is acidic and reacts with bases.

question_text: An iron nail is added to each of the two test tubes ‘P’ and ‘Q’ containing aqueous copper (II) sulphate, and aqueous silver nitrate respectively. Which of the following observation is correct?
options: In test tube ‘P’ iron nail is coated with a blue coating and in test tube ‘Q’ there is no reaction.
Iron nail is coated with a brown coating in test tube ‘P’ and silver coating in test tube ‘Q’.
There is no reaction in either of the test tubes ‘P’ or ‘Q’.
There is no reaction in test tube ‘P’ but a silver coating on iron nail is seen in test tube ‘Q’.
answer_text: Iron nail is coated with a brown coating in test tube ‘P’ and silver coating in test tube ‘Q’.
answer_explanation: Iron is more reactive than both copper and silver, so it displaces them from their salt solutions, depositing brown copper and grey-silver metal on the nail.

question_text: Methyl orange is added to dilute hydrochloric acid and to aqueous sodium hydroxide. What is the colour of the methyl orange in each solution? (Table: Sample | colour in dilute hydrochloric acid | colour in aqueous sodium hydroxide)
options: A: Orange in HCl, Red in NaOH
B: Red in HCl, Yellow in NaOH
C: Red in HCl, Orange in NaOH
D: Yellow in HCl, Red in NaOH
answer_text: B: Red in HCl, Yellow in NaOH
answer_explanation: Methyl orange is red in acidic solution and yellow in basic solution.

question_text: Which of the following substances when dissolved in equal volume of water, will have the highest pH value?
options: Sulphuric acid
Acetic acid
Magnesium hydroxide
Sodium hydroxide
answer_text: Sodium hydroxide
answer_explanation: Sodium hydroxide is a strong, highly soluble base and produces the greatest hydroxide-ion concentration among the choices.

question_text: When excess of carbon dioxide is passed through lime water, the milkiness disappears because
options: water soluble calcium carbonate converts to water soluble calcium bicarbonate.
insoluble calcium carbonate converts to water soluble calcium bicarbonate.
water soluble calcium carbonate converts to insoluble calcium bicarbonate.
insoluble calcium carbonate converts to insoluble calcium bicarbonate.
answer_text: insoluble calcium carbonate converts to water soluble calcium bicarbonate.
answer_explanation: Excess CO₂ converts the milky CaCO₃ precipitate into soluble Ca(HCO₃)₂, so the milkiness disappears.

question_text: In the reaction of aqueous solution of barium chloride with aqueous solution of sodium sulphate, the aqueous solution formed will be:
options: BaCl2
BaSO4
Na2SO4
NaCl
answer_text: NaCl
answer_explanation: BaCl₂(aq) + Na₂SO₄(aq) → BaSO₄(s) + 2NaCl(aq); barium sulphate precipitates and sodium chloride remains in solution.

question_text: Assertion (A): C4H8, C4H6 and C4H10 are members of the same homologous series Reason (R): C4H8, C4H6, C3H4, C3H6, C2H4, C2H2 are unsaturated hydrocarbons.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, and R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
answer_text: A is false but R is true.
answer_explanation: C₄H₁₀, C₄H₈ and C₄H₆ belong to different homologous series—alkanes, alkenes and alkynes. All compounds listed in the reason are unsaturated hydrocarbons.

question_text: The following activity is set-up in the science lab by the teacher. He clamped an aluminium wire on a stand and fixed a pin to the free end of the wire using wax. Then he heated the wire with a burner from the end where the wire is clamped. Students observed the pin fall off. A. If the teacher replaces aluminium wire by silver wire, will the students’ observation change? Justify your answer. B. Will the aluminium wire melt? Give reason for your answer.
answer_text:
A. The pin will still fall, and it may fall sooner because silver is a better conductor of heat than aluminium. Heat reaches the wax more rapidly and melts it.
B. The aluminium wire will not melt under normal heating in this activity. Its melting point is much higher than that of wax, so the wax melts and releases the pin first.
answer_explanation: Metals conduct heat, but different metals do so at different rates. Wax has a much lower melting point than aluminium.

question_text: Attempt either option A or B. A. An element ‘X’ is stored in kerosene, and cannot be extracted from its ore using a reducing agent. ‘X’ forms an ionic compound on reaction with chlorine. (i) Can we store ‘X’ in water? Give reason to support your answer. (ii) Identify element ‘X’. Name the process used and write the equat ion for extraction of ‘X’ from its ore. OR B. The domes of many building in Europe are made of copper. These domes now appear greenish in colour. (i) Why do the domes appear greenish though copper is orange -red in colour? (ii) In your opinion, should the copper domes be replaced by iron domes to overcome the problem of change of colour of copper domes? (iii) Domes used to be made from thin sheets of metals. Why did the ancient architects use copper to make domes?
answer_text:
Option A:
(i) X cannot be stored in water because it reacts vigorously with water, producing a hydroxide and hydrogen gas; the reaction may be highly exothermic.
(ii) X may be sodium. It is extracted by electrolytic reduction of molten sodium chloride (Downs process):
Cathode: Na⁺ + e⁻ → Na
Anode: 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻
Overall: 2NaCl(l) → 2Na(l) + Cl₂(g).

OR

Option B:
(i) Copper reacts slowly with moist air, CO₂ and O₂ to form a green patina of basic copper carbonate, CuCO₃·Cu(OH)₂.
(ii) No. Iron would rust and corrode progressively, whereas the copper patina is adherent and protects the underlying metal.
(iii) Copper is highly malleable, so it can be beaten into thin sheets; it is also durable and corrosion-resistant.
answer_explanation: Highly reactive metals cannot be reduced chemically and require electrolysis. Copper's protective patina and malleability make it suitable for long-lasting domes.

question_text: Amrita electrolysed distilled water using the set-up shown in figure 1. She was expecting two gases to be evolved at the anode and cathode respectively . Fig.1 Suddenly, she realised that the bulb in the circuit did not glow when she used distilled water (figure 2) Fig. 2 After this realization, she added a substance to the distilled water for electrolysis to take place. Answer the following questions based on the information given above: A. Which gas was she expecting to be formed at the anode and which one at the cathode respectively? B. Why did the bulb not glow when Amrita passed electricity through distilled water? C. Which substance was added by Amrita to distilled water to get the expected result? - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - For visually impaired students Identify the type of reaction: A. ZnO + C Zn + CO B. ZnCO3 heat ZnO + CO2 C. 2Mg + O2 2 MgO + heat
answer_text:
A. Oxygen is evolved at the anode and hydrogen at the cathode.
B. Distilled water contains too few ions and is therefore a very poor conductor, so the bulb does not glow.
C. A few drops of dilute sulphuric acid may be added to supply ions and increase conductivity.
Overall reaction: 2H₂O(l) → 2H₂(g) + O₂(g).
answer_explanation: Electrolysis needs mobile ions to carry electric current. Acidified water conducts and decomposes into hydrogen and oxygen in a 2:1 volume ratio.

question_text: Sara took 2 mL of dilute NaOH solution in a test tube and added two drops of phenolphthalein solution to it. The solution turned pink in colour. She added dilute H 2SO4 to the above solution drop by drop until the solution in the test tube became colourless. 40 drops of dilute H2SO4 were used for the change in . colour from pink to colourless. When Sara added a drop of NaOH to the solution, the colour changed to back to pink again. Sara now tried the activity with different volumes of NaOH and recorded her observation in the table given below: S. No. Volume of dil. NaOH taken (mL) Drops of dil. H2SO4 used 1 2 20 2 3 30 3 4 40 Answer the following questions based on the above information: A. If Sara used concentrated H2SO4 in place of dilute H2SO4, how many drops will be required for the change in colour to be observed? (a) 40 (b) < 40 (c) >40 Justify your answer. B. Sara measured 20 drops of dil. H2SO4 and found its volume to be 1 mL. If Sara observed a change in colour of NaoH solution by using 3 mL of H2SO4, how many mL of NaOH did she add to the test tube initially? OR Sara takes 10 drops of dilute H2SO4 in the test tube and adds two drops of phenolphthalein solution to it. Then she adds NaOH dropwise. Sara observes a change in colour after adding 20 drops of NaOH. What change in colour would she observe and why? C. Write a balanced chemical equation for the reaction taking place in the above experiment. Which of the following is true and why? The reaction is a (a) neutralisation and double displacement reaction (b) neutralisation and precipitation reaction (c) precipitation and double displacement reaction (d) neutralisation, double displacement as well as precipitation reaction.
answer_text:
A. Fewer than 40 drops will be required. Concentrated H₂SO₄ supplies more acid per drop, so a smaller volume neutralises the same NaOH.

B. 20 drops = 1 mL, so 3 mL H₂SO₄ = 60 drops. From the table, 10 drops of acid neutralise 1 mL of NaOH. Hence initial NaOH volume = 60/10 = 6 mL.

OR

Initially the acidic solution with phenolphthalein is colourless. On adding sufficient NaOH, it changes from colourless to pink because the solution becomes basic.

C. H₂SO₄ + 2NaOH → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O. It is (a) a neutralisation and double displacement reaction. Acid and base exchange ions to form salt and water; no insoluble precipitate is formed.
answer_explanation: The indicator changes according to pH, while the amount required depends on the relative quantities/concentrations of acid and base. Neutralisation here is also double displacement.

question_text: Attempt either option A or B. A. A hydrocarbon with the formula C xHy undergoes complete combustion as shown in the following equation: 2CxHy + 9O2 → 6CO2 + 6H2O. (a) What are the values of ‘x’ and ‘y’? (b) Give the chemical (IUPAC) name of the hydrocarbon. (c) Draw its electron dot structure. (d) Name the alcohol which on heating with conc. H2SO4 will produce the above hydrocarbon CxHy. . (e) Write a balanced chemical equation for the reaction of C xHy with hydrogen gas in presence of Nickel. OR B. The electronic structures of atoms P and Q are shown below Based on the information given above, answer the following questions: (a) If P and Q combine to form a compound, what type of bond is formed between them? (b) Give the chemical formula of the compound formed. (c) The compound so formed is dissolved in water. Is the resultant solution acidic or basic in nature? Justify your answer. (d) Write the chemical equation for the reaction between ‘Q’ and ethanol. (e) What will be the formula of the compound formed when ‘P’ undergoes bonding with carbon? - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - For visually impaired students A. A hydrocarbon with the formula CxHy undergoes complete combustion as shown in the following equation: 2CxHy + 9O2 → 6CO2 + 6H2O. (a) What are the values of ‘x’ and ‘y’? (b) Give the chemical (IUPAC) name of the hydrocarbon. (c) Is CxHy a saturated or an unsaturated hydrocarbon? (d) Name the alcohol which on heating with conc. H2SO4 will produce the above hydrocarbon CxHy. (e) Write a balanced chemical equation for the reaction of C xHy with hydrogen gas in presence of Nickel. OR B. Oxygen can combine with both metals and non -metals. It combines with Calcium to form CaO and with carbon to form CO2. (a) What type of bond is formed between carbon and oxygen? (b) Identify the type of bond formed between Calcium and oxygen. (c) Which of the above compounds will be a good conductor of electricity in molten state and why? (d) Comment on the physical state (solid, liquid or gas) of CaO and CO2. (e) What is the valency of carbon in CO2? . Section – C
answer_text:
Option A:
From 2CxHy + 9O2 → 6CO2 + 6H2O:
2x = 6 → x = 3; 2y = 12 → y = 6. Thus the hydrocarbon is C3H6, propene, an unsaturated hydrocarbon.
Electron-dot/structural representation: CH3–CH=CH2, with one shared electron pair in each single bond and two shared pairs in the C=C bond.
The alcohol is propanol; on dehydration with concentrated H2SO4 and heat:
CH3CH2CH2OH → CH3CH=CH2 + H2O.
Hydrogenation:
CH3CH=CH2 + H2 →[Ni] CH3CH2CH3.

OR (visually impaired option B):
(a) Carbon–oxygen bonds in CO2 are covalent.
(b) Calcium and oxygen form an ionic bond in CaO.
(c) Molten CaO conducts because its ions are free to move; CO2 does not have mobile ions.
(d) CaO is a solid with a strong ionic lattice; CO2 is a gas of small covalent molecules.
(e) Carbon has valency 4 in CO2.
answer_explanation: Balancing the combustion equation fixes the molecular formula. Propene undergoes dehydration formation from propanol and addition of hydrogen across its double bond.

question_text: Arnav was making notes and he wrote down the following statements from his understanding of reflection from curved surfaces. I. Concave mirrors can produce both real and virtual images depending on the position of the object. II. Convex mirrors always produce real, inverted images regardless of the object’s position. III. In both concave and convex mirrors, the image location can be determined using the mirror formula 1/f = 1/v + 1/u where f is the focal length, v is the image distance, and u is the object distance. Choose from the following the correct option that lists the correct statements about reflection from curved surfaces.
options: I and II
I, II and III
II and III
I and III
answer_text: I and III
answer_explanation: A concave mirror may form real or virtual images, whereas a convex mirror always forms a virtual, erect image. The mirror formula 1/f = 1/v + 1/u applies to both types.

question_text: Choose the correct option from the below which explains the reason for us to perceive the day sky as blue.
options: As sunlight passes through the atmosphere, shorter wavelengths, such as blue are scattered more than other colors.
The sky appears blue because all colors are scattered equally, but blue light is stronger and more visible to the human eye.
The blue color of the sky is due to longer wavelengths like red and orange scattering more than shorter wavelengths, making blue stand out more.
The atmosphere contains blue-colored particles that give the sky its blue appearance.
answer_text: As sunlight passes through the atmosphere, shorter wavelengths, such as blue are scattered more than other colors.
answer_explanation: Rayleigh scattering is much stronger for shorter wavelengths, so blue light is scattered throughout the sky more than red light.

question_text: Assertion (A): A point object is placed at a distance of 26 cm from a convex mirror of focal length 26 cm. The image will not form at infinity. Reason (R): For above given system the equation 1/f = 1/v + 1/u gives v = ∞.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, and R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
answer_text: A is true but R is false.
answer_explanation: For a convex mirror, f = +26 cm and u = −26 cm. Using 1/f = 1/v + 1/u gives v = +13 cm, so the image is finite and not at infinity.

question_text: For visually impaired students: A. Under what conditions can a convex lens form a virtual image? B. Why does a piece of paper catch fire if we allow sunlight to pass through a convex lens onto the paper?
answer_text:
A. A convex lens forms a virtual image when the object is placed between the optical centre and the principal focus — the image is virtual, erect and magnified.
B. The convex lens converges sunlight to a tiny, intense focal spot, concentrating enough heat there to ignite the paper.
answer_explanation: A convex lens only forms a virtual image for an object closer than its focal length; when parallel rays (like sunlight) converge at the focus, the concentrated energy raises the temperature enough to burn paper.

question_text: For visually impaired students: A. You are given four resistors each having resistance of R ohm. Find the maximum and minimum resistance that can be made with these four resistors. OR B. A copper wire has a length L=2 m, a cross-sectional area A=0.5 mm², and resistivity ρ=1.7×10⁻⁸ Ω-m. Calculate the resistance of another wire made of the same material whose length is twice the length of the wire but has the same cross-sectional area.
answer_text:
A. Maximum resistance = 4R (all four in series); minimum resistance = R/4 (all four in parallel).

OR

B. New length = 4 m, area = 0.5 mm² = 0.5×10⁻⁶ m²; R = ρL/A = (1.7×10⁻⁸×4)/(0.5×10⁻⁶) = 0.136 Ω.
answer_explanation: Series resistances add directly (maximum); parallel combination gives the smallest equivalent resistance (minimum). Resistance is directly proportional to length for a uniform wire, so doubling length doubles resistance.

question_text: For visually impaired students: (i) What is dispersion of light? (ii) Explain the condition under which dispersion happens. (iii) Give one reason that causes presbyopia.
answer_text:
(i) Dispersion is the splitting of white light into its constituent colours (a spectrum).
(ii) It occurs when polychromatic (white) light passes through a refracting medium, such as a prism, whose refractive index differs for different wavelengths, so each colour bends by a different amount.
(iii) Presbyopia is caused by weakening of the ciliary muscles and/or reduced flexibility of the eye lens with age.
answer_explanation: Different wavelengths of light bend by different amounts (different refractive indices) in a medium like glass, separating white light into its component colours. Presbyopia is an age-related loss of the eye's power of accommodation.

question_text: A student needs to make a 0.12 Ω resistor. She has some copper wire of 0.80 mm diameter. Resistivity of copper is 1.8 × 10−8 Ωm (i) Determine the cross-sectional area of the wire. (ii) Calculate the length of wire required for the 0.12 Ω resistor.
answer_text:
Diameter d = 0.80 mm, so radius r = 0.40 mm = 4.0×10⁻⁴ m.
(i) Cross-sectional area A = πr² = π(4.0×10⁻⁴)² = 5.03×10⁻⁷ m² (approximately).
(ii) Using R = ρL/A,
L = RA/ρ = (0.12×5.03×10⁻⁷)/(1.8×10⁻⁸) ≈ 3.35 m.
Therefore, required length ≈ 3.35 m.
answer_explanation: The wire area is calculated from its radius, and the resistivity relation R = ρL/A then gives the required length.

question_text: Magnetic field lines are shown in the given diagram. A student makes a statement that the magnetic field at X is stronger than at Y. (i) Explain with reason if the student’s claim is correct. (ii) Also redraw the diagram and mark the direction of magnetic field lines.
answer_text: The general answer without the diagram's exact spacing: magnetic field strength at a point is indicated by how closely spaced the field lines are there — closer lines mean a stronger field. Field lines outside a magnet run from the north pole to the south pole. Whether X is actually stronger than Y depends on the line spacing shown in the diagram, which is not available here.
answer_explanation: Field-line density represents magnetic field strength — this rule lets a student evaluate the claim once they see the actual spacing at X and Y in the diagram.

question_text: The above image is that of a Digital Single Lense Reflector (DSLR) Camera which are used to take high resolution photographs by professional photographers. The second image of the above two is a schematic diagram of how an image is formed on the sensor of the camera. Based on your understanding of the lenses, answer the following questions. A. What type of lens is used in the DSLR camera shown in the image? B. What type of image is formed on the sensor? Attempt either subpart C or D. C. A photographer is using a DSLR camera with a lens of focal length f=50 mm to take a close-up photograph of a small object. The lens projects an image onto the camera sensor that is located 60 mm behind the lens. Calculate the object distance (i.e., the distance between the object and the lens). . OR D. A photographer is using a DSLR camera to take a picture of a flower. The flower is positioned 150 mm away from the camera lens. The actual height of the flower is 80 mm, and the image height formed on the camera’s sensor is measured to be 20 mm. Calculate the focal length of the camera lens. For visually impaired students Zarina worked as an apprentice in a factory where flashlights and solar cookers are made. She learnt to make the circuits, the design of the light-box and light concentrators of the solar cookers as well. She learnt the uses of lenses in making all those tools. Based on your understanding of lenses, answer the following questions. A. What kind of lenses are used in the flashlight and light concentrator of the solar-cooker? B. Give reasons for your choices in your answer for part A. Attempt either subpart C or D. C. An object is placed 40 cm away from a lens which is normally used in a solar-cooker. The image formed is twice the size of the object. Calculate the focal length of the lens. OR D. An object is placed 20 cm in front of a lens which is used in a flashlight, and the image is formed 10 cm away from the lens on the same side as the object. Calculate the focal length of the lens.
answer_text:
A. A convex (converging) lens is used.
B. The sensor receives a real, inverted and generally diminished image.
C. Given f = +50 mm and v = +60 mm. Using 1/f = 1/v − 1/u:
1/50 = 1/60 − 1/u
→1/u = 1/50 − 1/60 = 1/300
Therefore u = −300 mm; object distance = 300 mm.

OR

D. u = −150 mm, object height = 80 mm and inverted image height = −20 mm. Magnification m = hi/ho = −20/80 = −1/4 = v/u, so v = 37.5 mm.
1/f = 1/v − 1/u = 1/37.5 + 1/150 = 1/30.
Therefore f = 30 mm.
answer_explanation: A camera requires a converging lens to form a real image on its sensor. The lens formula and magnification relation provide the distances and focal length.

question_text: For visually impaired students: A. (i) Explain why in household circuits only the fuse is connected in series with all the rest of the appliances but all appliances are connected in parallel to each other. (ii) In a household circuit, an electric heater of power 1500 W and a fan of power 500 W are connected in parallel to a 220 V supply. A fuse rated for 10 A is connected to the circuit to protect it from excessive current. (a) Calculate the total current drawn by the heater and the fan. (b) Determine whether the 10 A fuse is appropriate for this circuit or if it will blow. OR B. Two resistors, R1=6 Ω and R2=12 Ω, are connected in parallel to a 24V battery. The circuit operates for 5 minutes. (i) Calculate the total heat generated in both resistors. (ii) If each resistor has a power rating of 100 W, determine whether it is safe to use these resistors in the circuit.
answer_text:
Option A:
(i) A fuse is connected in series so the entire circuit current passes through it and it can break the circuit during an overload. Appliances are connected in parallel so each receives the full 220 V and can operate independently of the others.
(ii)(a) Total power = 1500 + 500 = 2000 W. Total current I = P/V = 2000/220 ≈ 9.09 A.
(b) A 10 A fuse is appropriate — normal operating current (≈9.09 A) is below 10 A, so it should not blow during normal operation.

OR

Option B:
R1 = 6 Ω and R2 = 12 Ω are in parallel across 24 V for t = 5 min = 300 s.
P1 = V²/R1 = 24²/6 = 96 W; P2 = V²/R2 = 24²/12 = 48 W.
Total heat H = (P1 + P2)×t = 144×300 = 43,200 J.
Both are safe at 24 V because 96 W and 48 W are each below the 100 W power rating.
answer_explanation: Series fusing protects the whole circuit while parallel wiring keeps each appliance independent and at full voltage. Power dissipated in each parallel resistor is V²/R, and total heat follows H = Pt.
